title: Taiwanese American Center of Northern California 北加州台灣會館
content_html:
The Taiwanese American Center of Northern California (北加州台灣會館, TAC) is a non-profit community organization founded in 2003 to serve as a gathering place and resource center for Taiwanese Americans in the San Francisco Bay Area. Based in San Jose, the center operates out of an 8,600-square-foot facility in the Silicon Valley area and provides a wide range of educational, cultural, and civic programs.

The idea for the center took shape in 2001 when Dr. 張信行 (Chang Hsin-Hsing) and his wife 黃美星 began hosting monthly gatherings with a group of like-minded community members to discuss establishing a permanent home for Taiwanese Americans in Northern California. The preparatory committee was formally established on February 16, 2003, with Dr. Chang serving as founding convener. The center opened its first location in Fremont on May 1, 2003, and held its formal inauguration ceremony on September 27, 2003, receiving congratulatory plaques from Taiwan’s President Chen Shui-bian, Vice President Lu Hsiu-lien, and other officials. In 2004, the Taiwan School was established with support from National Taiwan Normal University Professor Yu Po-chuan, offering Mandarin, Taiwanese, Hakka, and arts instruction. The center relocated to its current address at 4413 Fortran Court, San Jose in May 2009.

The center operates a Taiwan School (台灣學校) offering language and cultural classes for children and adults, and a Taiwan Center for Mandarin Learning (臺灣華語文學習中心, TCML) that extends into mainstream institutions including the San Francisco Public Library system. Weekly programming includes health lectures, community talks, a seniors program, and performing arts. The center has hosted delegations from Taiwan’s government and received recognition from the Overseas Community Affairs Council for its cultural preservation work.
